title: [Benchmark] 3x Tesla V100 32GB (sm_70, PCIe 3.0), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash IST-DAS-2.00bpw, Windows source build 7dd5cf1 - and a multi-instance wedging note
body:
First DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash numbers on **sm_70 (Volta) + Windows**: the source build works on V100 - relevant to #3935, since the prebuilt feed's cuda13 packages (sm_86/sm_120) can never cover Volta, and CUDA 12.x source is the only path there.

## Build (sm_70, Windows)

- Source `7dd5cf1` (v0.2.4.2), `-DSTRATA_BUILD_DSV41=ON -DSTRATA_NATIVE_EXPERTS=ON`, CUDA 12.4, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=native` with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2` (three V100s -> sm_70 only)
- The pre-sm_80 legacy path engages as designed: `exl3: CUDA0/1/2 decodes with v1.1.8's kernels`
- One build hiccup: link.exe failed with `LNK1104: cannot open %TEMP%\lnk{...}.tmp` until TMP was moved off the user temp dir - likely an AV interference, not a Strata issue.

Setup with already-downloaded files worked end to end: `setup.py --family deepseek41 --model IST-DAS-2.00bpw --gguf-dir ...` verified the 249 GB of shards and the Engram table against their SHA-256, fetched the 8 GB DSpark drafter, packed 48,488 tensors, and its test question passed. The engine runs from `STRATA_DSV41_EXE`/`engine-dsv41\`.

## Numbers (3x V100, engine-line totals: generated tokens / whole wall time)

IST-DAS-2.00bpw, context 8192 (default), `--dspark auto`, layer split auto [0,42]/[13,26]/[27,39] + head (`--tp 2` falls back, same as maya-ds4: the experts' 256-value blocks split n_ff 2304 no other way):

| | tok/s |
|---|---:|
| 1024-token answers, warm | 17.4 |
| 3072-token answers, warm | **22.0** |
| math probe (~2.2k tokens, reasoning on) | 20.9 |
| prefill, ~7k-token prompt (engine line) | 176 |
| DSpark drafts kept | 86-94% |

Expert placement at start: 9,333 of 15,360 experts in VRAM (28 GB per card, 3x 32 GB full), 4,416 hot experts pre-read into the 48 GB RAM store, 6,411 streamed in place; the CPU lane settles at 2-6% of the experts when warm.

For the docs' reference machines: this is ~3x an RTX 3060 12 GB (7.2) and ~4.7x an RTX 5070 (4.7) on decode, with the same streaming design but 3x the VRAM and 128 GB of RAM.

## Same box, same model, the Maya engine

For completeness - the same PC also runs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Project Maya's `maya-ds4` (v1.1.26, the engine this one is ported from) with Maya-S, its own mixed quant (Q6_K dense + IQ2/IQ3 experts) where all CPU-lane experts are pinned in RAM:

| | strata-dsv41 0.1.49.2 (2.00bpw, streaming) | maya-ds4 v1.1.26 (Maya-S, pinned) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 3072-token answers | 22.0 | 27.5 |
| 1024-token answers | 17.4 | 24.2 |
| prefill ~7k | 176 | 425 |

The streaming design trades some speed for its 46 GB-RAM entry point - both engines answer the same hard math probe correctly (n! with 2019 trailing zeros -> 8090, with a Legendre-formula proof), on both engines.

## One thing that may be worth a guard: multiple instances wedge each other's expert placement

Three copies of the start script were allowed to run at once (Windows asked "run this?" for each). The copy that survived had measured VRAM *while the others still held it*, concluded there was no room, and put **all 15,744 experts on the CPU lane** - 2.5 tok/s, 3-4 GB used per card - while a single clean start lands 9,333 experts in VRAM as above. It self-heals with a single-instance restart, but a lock file or a "another engine holds the GPUs" check at start would save Volta/small-VRAM users a confusing first impression.

## Machine

- 3x Tesla V100-PCIE-32GB (two 72-SM "PG500-216" + one 80-SM V100), PCIe 3.0 x16 each, TCC, driver 582.78, CUDA 12.4
- 2x Xeon E5-2696 v3, 128 GB DDR3L-1600, Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC
- Model + pack on a Kingston NV2 1 TB NVMe; page file 112 GB
